claim: Le Castellet is officially classified as one of the Plus Beaux Villages de France, a perched medieval village near Bandol with a 12th-century church (Église de la Transfiguration-du-Sauveur) enlarged in the 18th century, ramparts with a viewpoint, and locations from Pagnol's La Femme du Boulanger.
quote: Le Castellet (Var), l'un des Plus Beaux Villages de France autour de Bandol… Église du XIIème siècle agrandie au XVIIIème par une deuxième nef et une sacristie… La place de l'Ormeau et la crêperie du Roy d'Ys accueillent d'ailleurs des répliques cultes

claim: In summer 1938 Marcel Pagnol filmed La Femme du Boulanger in Le Castellet, using the Place de l'Ormeau, Rue Droite, the Portail, Rue de la Poste, the church, and Angèle's house at 6 Rue de l'Aube as sets.
quote: À l'été 1938, Marcel Pagnol accompagné de sa troupe s'installe dans la propriété de Raimu à Bandol et choisit le village du Castellet comme décor de son film… la première scène du film a été tournée Place de l'Ormeau

claim: La Cadière-d'Azur is a perched Provençal village on a cliff opposite Le Castellet (~5 km away) with a 360° panorama over Bandol vineyards toward the Mediterranean, the Sainte-Baume massif and the bay of La Ciotat, first recorded in 977.
quote: La Cadière-d'Azur is perched on the edge of its cliff, on a hill opposite the village of Castellet, and benefits from a panorama that goes right to the shores of the Mediterranean

claim: The Rade de Toulon is the largest bay in Europe by water surface area, formed 8,000 years ago when post-glacial sea level rise flooded the valley between Mont Faron and Saint-Mandrier; it is divided into Petite Rade and Grande Rade and hosts France's main naval base.
quote: La rade de Toulon est la plus grande rade d'Europe par sa superficie en eau. Elle s'est formée il y a 8 000 ans, lors de la remontée du niveau de la mer consécutive à la fin de la dernière glaciation

claim: Mont Faron rises to 584 m above Toulon and is reached by a unique-on-the-Mediterranean cable car that climbs to the summit in a few minutes, where the WWII Mémorial du Débarquement de Provence and the Zoo du Faron are located.
quote: Le mont Faron, qui culmine à 584 mètres, domine la ville de Toulon… Le téléphérique, unique sur le littoral méditerranéen, permet d'atteindre le sommet en quelques minutes

claim: The Musée National de la Marine in Toulon is housed in the former Arsenal at Place Monsenergue, Quai de Norfolk, and tells the maritime history of the city through naval models, paintings and arsenal artefacts.
quote: Place Monsenergue, Quai de Norfolk, 83000 Toulon… musée national de la Marine de Toulon

claim: Toulon's Provençal market on Cours Lafayette stretches roughly 1 km and runs every morning except Monday from 7:30 to 12:30, with an additional non-food market in the afternoon Monday to Saturday.
quote: Le marché du cours Lafayette long d'1 km… alimentaire ouvert tous les matins sauf le lundi de 7h30 à 12h30

claim: Marcel Pagnol was born 28 February 1895 in a bourgeois house on Cours Barthélemy in Aubagne; the ground floor (130 m²) is now a museum with a reconstituted family apartment, exhibition rooms and a 20-seat projection room.
quote: Marcel Pagnol was born on 28 February 1895 in a 19th-century bourgeois house on the Cours Barthélemy in Aubagne… The ground floor of the house can be visited (130 m²)

claim: Le Petit Monde de Marcel Pagnol in Aubagne stages Pagnol's universe with around 200 clay santons sculpted by Aubagne santonniers as a tribute to their native son, now displayed at the Atelier Thérèse Neveu.
quote: En 1974, les crèchistes et santonniers d'Aubagne… 200 santons mettent en scène la vie et l'œuvre de l'écrivain-cinéaste

claim: The Chapelle Notre-Dame du Beausset-Vieux is a 12th-century Romano-Provençal chapel perched at 383 m altitude near Le Beausset, listed as a National Historical Monument since 1970, with a Virgin statue carved in 1712 in Pierre Puget's Toulon workshop and ex-votos by Eusèbe Nicolas.
quote: Notre Dame du Beausset Vieux… construite au XIIe siècle… à 383 mètres d'altitude offre un panorama remarquable sur les villages perchés de l'ouest toulonnais et le vignoble de Bandol

claim: Sanary-sur-Mer was dubbed by Ludwig Marcuse the world capital of artistic and literary exile; between 1933 and 1940 it hosted Thomas Mann, Lion Feuchtwanger and other German intellectuals fleeing the Nazi book burnings, and a memorial plaque was installed in 1987 (updated 2011).
quote: the journalist Ludwig Marcuse awarded Sanary the honorary title of 'world capital of artistic and literary exile'… Between 1933 and 1940 this small Côte d'Azur fishing village hosted German intellectuals

claim: Sanary's Parcours des Exilés is an 8 km walking route with 21 commemorative plaques (QR-coded in three languages) marking the residences of about thirty exiled German-language writers including Feuchtwanger, Werfel, Schickelé and Brecht, who reportedly finished work on The Threepenny Opera from port cafés here.
quote: le 'Parcours des Exilés', une promenade de huit kilomètres jalonnée de plaques… C'est sur la terrasse de Brecht, ou dans l'un des cafés du port, qu'il termina L'Opéra de quat'sous

claim: Ollioules, at the entrance of its eponymous gorges a few km from Toulon, holds the national 'Ville et Métiers d'Art' label and hosts around thirty craft workshops (stained glass, mosaic, sculpture, ceramics), with a Saint-Laurent church and the remains of a feudal castle dominating the old town.
quote: Ollioules est labellisée 'Ville et Métiers d'Art'… une trentaine d'artisans d'art… le château féodal, l'église Saint-Laurent et un important noyau médiéval

claim: The Abbaye Saint-Michel-de-Frigolet is a Premonstratensian abbey in the Montagnette near Tarascon in Bouches-du-Rhône, well outside the 30 km radius of Le Castellet (Tarascon is over 130 km away by road).
quote: L'abbaye Saint-Michel de Frigolet est une abbaye de chanoines prémontrés, située près de Tarascon, dans la Montagnette, dans le département des Bouches-du-Rhône

claim: Aubagne stages a Santon and Ceramics Market twice a year (summer and Christmas), with the Christmas edition running from mid-November to late December, gathering clay artisans in the town centre and reinforcing the town's claim as a capital of santon-making.
quote: Twice a year, in summer and at Christmas time, santon makers and ceramists settle in the centre of Aubagne for this claywork market
